notes: Settings: Always on (start with Windows, stay awake), Claude Code, Security (rotate all keys), Publishing, Browser and computer.
The expanded model bar shows each model's level, sign-in state, health and address.
Who picks the model: Jev, Kev, Fastino GLiDE, GLiNER2.5-Decide and Not Diamond, and they learn from your changed picks and replies.
Share a message into another project's memory; publish pages; Chrome and computer use.
This update window: what's new, app updates, new models and Hermes releases.
Long chats shrink like Claude Code and Codex and stay alive.
No checks on read-only commands, so tools run faster.
Setup wizard: closing it ends it.
A lost reply is always recovered, and a closed Claude never holds its chat.
After a restart, waiting messages pause for one click.
Apps: a background watch suggests updates for each app.
The update watch follows your brief, reads videos by what is said, and shows its progress live.
The update watch's model picker sits beside frequency and Check now.
The update watch uses your connected models, Claude included.
Every model plans first and waits for GO before building.
Any file you drop gets into the chat.
A message sent while models load waits, then goes.
Faster tools: each window gets only the tools it shows, and lookups read only the rows they need.
Every model searches with rg.
A message stuck on Checking plugins ends after 60 s and names the step that stuck.
A new turn engine: Claude's own events decide when a chat is busy, so chats no longer stall.
Messages go to the model at once, and Stop stops only the running reply.
Every wait names its reason.
Themes: Black, High contrast and Warm paper join Dark and Light.
Appearance: Text size scales the whole app, and a Font menu lists the fonts Windows has, starting on Helvetica.
Messages typed while one is being prepared join it as one message.
A command waiting for Allow no longer holds up other chats.
While a message is routed, its label names who picks, then the model picked.
Trismegistus is now Ghidorah. Same chats, keys and settings; the III icon stays.
A message you add mid-reply shows where the model read it.
Models can rename apps and change their icons.
One GO covers every step of the job you approved.
Preview pages sit in the right place and open inside Ghidorah or in your browser.
Fork works again: background updates no longer leave rows that block it.
Only your words go into a running reply, so a question mid-job no longer ends the job.
Sends never wait for a summary, Hermes keeps its session, and plugins are checked only when they change.
Claude subscription models can write the routing summary.
The chat fills the window when the pane beside it is hidden.
In Bypass, a model starts Claude, Codex or Gemini without asking.
One look across the whole app: every screen uses the same colours, sizes and parts, in all five themes.
Title bar: Chat files, Export and Keyboard shortcuts sit in a menu after the chat title; the panels are one row of icons.
Under the message box: Attach, Voice, Dictate and Skills are icons; one line of controls with real switches and a context ring with its percent; the model pills sit on one line.
Sidebar: app tiles two to a row, one style for every heading, a dot on the right for unread chats.
Settings: search the sections; every setting is one row.
Export and Share no longer scroll sideways; Keyboard shortcuts and the window buttons follow light themes.
Sign in to Claude Code from Ghidorah: a button in Settings › Connections › Anthropic and on the Claude Code page.
When Claude Code is signed out, Ghidorah says so.
Ghidorah updates itself: it checks 4 s after it starts and every 3 hours, and downloads in the background.
A chip in the title bar shows the download, then restart to update. Click it, or just quit: the update installs then. Ghidorah never restarts by itself.
This window opens once after each update with what's new, and every version back to 0.1.0 in one scroll.
Your chats are copied before every install; the newest three copies stay beside your chats.
If a new version doesn't open, the one before comes back by itself, and this window says so.
Every version is on the public releases page, with a Download for Windows button. The installer asks where Ghidorah goes, and updates land there.
Ghidorah is open source: the code, the README and the installer now live in one place, github.com/koan-shdw/ghidorah.
Updates now come from that repository.
Hovering a model shows its limits the same way as the Context window.
A command in one chat no longer holds up your other chats.
Text a model writes between its tool steps now stays in the reply.
In a job window, Stop and send correction stops the run and sends, as it says.
Long chat summaries pick up where they left off instead of starting over.
A reply's actions now sit in one list: folded to "Ran 12 actions", or the current step while it works. Open a row to see its command and output.
On an app's page its latest chat glows, and a pill in the title bar opens that chat.

Screen control: a model can work in your apps and Chrome. It asks before each new app and before the whole screen, a bar shows while it works, and Esc stops it. Turn it on or off in Settings, Browser and computer.
Start a message with ?? to ask about the work in progress. A side model answers above the message box while the main model keeps going.
Share pages with clients: set it up once in Settings, Share with clients. Each project gets a private link, and client notes come back to the chat.
Ask a model for a page and it opens as a card under the reply, private until you share it, with Open, Open in browser and Copy link.
Long command output no longer weighs down the window; an action loads its full output when you open it.
After a Hermes model patches a file, it can edit that file again without reading it first.
In parallel work, Claude jobs get your message once, not twice.

Handover mode: Hand off (in the chat menu, or type /handoff) has the chat write a handover. START HANDOVER under it opens the next chat in the series, numbered, with the same settings, and keeps the old chat beside it in Plan mode.
During a handover, Show old chat and Send to new chat move only what is new between the two chats. Close handover unpins the old chat and gives it its own mode back.
The first time a chat's context is compressed, a chip by the context ring suggests a handoff.
Delete now cancels a chat's queued messages and stops its running work instead of refusing. The dialog says so first.
Share with clients sets up when your Cloudflare sign-in reaches more than one account: it picks the one named after your email, or lets you choose.
Replies show their plan as a checklist at the top, ticked off as the model works and folded to "4 of 4 steps done" when it ends. Hermes models can now keep a task list too.
Handover mode: the old chat's comments finish on their own; it no longer asks to leave Plan mode after each one.
Switching ChatGPT accounts no longer waits on messages paused by a restart, and says which chat is still working.
Switching chats and opening a split or pane is about ten times faster on a long history.
Typing in a long chat no longer lags: only the message that changed redraws.
Streamed replies are saved in batches, so a long reply no longer slows the app.
Sends and tool results read only their own chat, not the whole history.
Claude Code works again when its usage check is slow; only the usage line says it is unavailable.
Claude Code is only in Connections, Anthropic: sign-in, plan and usage in one place.
Saving an app no longer fails with chat not found after a linked chat was deleted.
The sidebar button says New chat.
Images can use your ChatGPT sign-in: choose OpenAI, ChatGPT sign-in in Settings, Images. No API key needed.
A new chat started while an app is selected in the sidebar belongs to that app: the model starts with its repositories and repo map.
After a restart, a routed message waits for Claude Code to connect instead of holding its chat.
Connectors: Settings, MCP connections has Discover, with one-click sign-in for Webflow, Klaviyo, Notion, Linear, Stripe, PayPal, Zapier and more, plus search of the public MCP Registry.
Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides) for every model, with a guided setup.
Claude chats can use your claude.ai connectors: Connections, Anthropic. Each use still asks for approval.
An MCP server with a short setting such as DEBUG=1 no longer stalls MCP connections.
Settings has its own MCP section, under Tools after Plugins. Connections now lists only model suppliers.
Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides) is one click: Settings, MCP, Discover, Add. Google sign-in opens the first time a chat uses it.
Remote: each new chat gets its own topic in your Telegram bot chat. A message sent in a topic goes to that chat, and its replies, approvals and questions come back in the same topic.
Pinned chats' topics start with a pin, and desktop messages and replies are copied into the chat's topic. Turn it off in Settings, Remote, One topic per chat.
Telegram again refuses requests to open your saved secrets, instead of asking for a code.
Settings has one button: the cog at the bottom of the left rail. The Settings row with its second cog is gone.
Remote: the One topic per chat switch in Settings works again, and the topic error tells you to tap Start in your bot's Telegram chat.
Claude models: a short startup list no longer hides Fable.

Dictation works like Claude's: tap the mic or press Ctrl+D to start and again to finish, or hold either and let go. Your words appear live where the cursor was. X or Esc cancels, the check or Enter finishes without sending. Right-click the mic for microphone, language and Hold to record.

Dictation is much faster: the speech model stays loaded, and Whisper Large v3 Turbo is the new recommended model (Settings, Voice, Install speech). With an NVIDIA graphics card, Settings, Voice offers Use graphics card for many times faster dictation.
New chats open at once: the Ghidorah artwork is ready ahead of time, with no placeholder first.
Updates and restarts never make your connections look gone: suppliers, DeepSeek, ChatGPT and Claude show as they were, marked Checking..., until their checks answer.
Ghidorah starts faster: chat project folders refresh in the background instead of before the backend starts.
Updates put back any Ghidorah shortcut the installer removes, such as the desktop shortcut.
Fable 5.1 is back: Claude Code renamed it, and your defaults, favourites and chats now follow Claude Code's renames automatically.
Ghidorah no longer closes by itself or freezes while you type: tool outputs are saved once, in their own table, and nothing reads them all at once.
Whole tool outputs are kept 14 days: after that the first 2,000 characters stay, and opening the row says the rest was removed.
The chat file is reorganised in the background on the first start after this update, a few rows at a time.
Everything is quicker: each change reaches the window on its own instead of the whole chat state every time, so chat switches and typing no longer stall.

A message Claude's usage limit stops waits instead of failing: its row says Paused until 14:00, limit. Resumes by itself, and it is sent again at that time, also after a restart. Stop on the message cancels the wait.
A message typed while a reply runs is yours again if that reply fails: it goes back to the queue and is sent on, or asks you for a model.
A message whose model is blocked by its account asks you to choose a model instead of waiting for it to connect.

Long picture jobs no longer fill the disk or slow the start: a picture a model reads is saved as its file, not a copy. Copies already saved are cleared in the background after this update, a few rows at a time.
Deleting a chat is instant: Ghidorah goes straight to that chat's rows instead of reading every chat.
Telegram: a message typed into a chat's topic reaches that chat. Before, it was answered with That message is no longer waiting for a reply.
A newer Claude model takes the place of the one you picked: Fable 5.2 replaces Fable 5.1 in your defaults, favourites and chats, once. Link Fable 5.1 again and it stays.
A Claude message waits only when Claude itself refuses it. A usage meter at full no longer holds messages on its own, so an account without a 5-hour limit is never held by one.
Usage credits show in the usage panel for each account: on or off, why they are off, and what is spent. ChatGPT also shows the credits left and the resets you have saved.

The Resets and credits button opens the account's own usage page, from the usage panel and from a message waiting on a limit. Use a reset or switch on credits there and the waiting message goes by itself.
A full ChatGPT window no longer holds a message while the account has credits left.
Claude's 5-hour limit is now named Current session, as on Claude's own usage page.
The update window closes again. It says which version is installed and what's new, with one Close button. Before, Close did nothing while wake-word listening was on.
App updates, Hermes releases and the check for new models are in Settings › Updates. A dot on Settings and on Updates shows while a Hermes release waits for Roll in or Skip.

Voices: Kokoro reads replies aloud on this PC. Install it once in Settings › Voice, then press Listen under a reply or switch on Speak replies. The Voices window keeps your voices, and an app can have its own.
Listening: choose what hears your dictation in Settings › Voice or the setup wizard. Whisper on this PC, or Deepgram or ElevenLabs on your own key, which is tried before it is saved.
Waves while you dictate: bars beside the buttons or a line across the message box. Choose in Settings › Voice.
Dictation keeps your first and last words, and Done waits for a long recording instead of giving up.
Side chats: Discard asks first, and Send to main chat puts a summary in the main chat's message box. A branch, a side chat and a handover show the same bar at the top of the chat.

Zonos 3 Mini can read replies aloud through Zyphra Cloud on your own key. Choose it beside Kokoro in Settings › Voice › Reply voice and pick one of its ten voices. The key is tried before it is saved, and your voice's effects still apply.
Latest updates on an app's page: Add to to-dos makes a to-do from each ticked update, to work on later.
Bypass asks before a model reads Ghidorah's own data or your saved keys. Everything else in Bypass still runs without asking.
Turning on the wake word works again. Before, it was refused with Stop active work before restarting.
Restore, compact, fork, archive, handover and delete no longer stop at Inspect uncertain actions, and goals no longer pause there. Unfinished actions settle by themselves first.
A chat with a video and another model picked asks you to choose Gemini when Gemini is connected, instead of telling you to connect it.
After a model switch the new model is told once. Before, GPT was told twice.
Plugin commands send with no model connected, the usage panel fits a small window, and changing a project's mode no longer fails now and then.
The Show all chats button is gone: the Chats button on the rail clears an app's filter.

Subscriptions: Settings › Subscriptions lists every connection with what it costs a month, what is left and where the month's tokens went, by day, model and app. Type a price into a row to confirm it. A row opens to its limits and the supplier's own billing and usage pages.
Agents at work show as pills at the top right of the chat, each with its step, its time and a stop square. One that asks for a permission turns amber and takes Allow once or Deny right there.

Send now: a message sent while a reply runs waits in a dashed bubble. Send now on it, or Ctrl+Enter, stops the reply and sends it. A Send now switch in the chat bar makes that what Enter does, and Settings › General sets it for new chats.

The Workspace panel opens on sections: folder and branch, context, plan, changed files, saved outputs, agents and background work. Files, Changes, Terminal and Preview open from its Tools rows or the title bar, with a way back. The tabs are gone.
Kimi K3.1's thinking levels show as low, high and max.

Subscriptions: the list at the top of the page is gone. A row with no price has a small amber mark and a box to type the price into, in the row itself. A price that is there is clicked to change it, and a limit that is nearly used up has the same mark.

Telegram: every chat has its own thread in the bot chat, with a short name the sidebar shows too. A text in a thread goes to that chat, and a text in the main view starts a new one. A deleted or archived chat's thread goes with it.

Telegram: the reply shows in its thread while it is written, with Stop. Your text gets a mark when Ghidorah has it and another when it is answered. Long replies come whole, and texts sent while Ghidorah was closed are handled when it starts.

Telegram: a thread's icon shows its chat working, needing you or held by the usage limit. Home, pinned in the main view, lists them with a link to each thread. A reply's plan shows as a checklist, with Stop the agents.
Telegram: a voice note becomes your message, heard by Whisper on this PC, and the thread shows what was heard. A photo or a file goes into the chat as an attachment.
Telegram: a message sounds only when work ends or needs you, and never while you are at the PC.
Work a usage limit stopped, agents included, carries on by itself a minute after the reset. In Telegram the chat's thread says when, with Don’t carry on. Stop calls it off.
Settings › Remote: Make all threads again, for a clean start after you clear the bot's chat in Telegram, and a switch for the state on the thread icon.

The chat's controls sit in one row inside the message box: +, the mode and the models on the left, the context ring, Options, the microphone and send on the right. + holds Attach files, Skills and commands, Side chat, Voice helper and Add a model. Options holds the chat view, Send now, wake-ups, Speak replies and more.
One Workspace switch at the right of a chat's title bar opens the panel or closes it. A dot on it means files changed, an output was saved or an agent finished since you last looked.
Dictation: Enter or the send arrow finishes it, waits for your last words and sends. Esc cancels, and a second press on the microphone stops and leaves the words unsent.

Every model in a chat stays a chip in the message box. When they don't fit they wrap onto more lines instead of folding into one chip, and in a narrow chat they take a line of their own above the buttons.
Anthropic: Switch account works again after a sign-in page was left open, with Cancel sign-in while it waits
Anthropic: new Sign out button
Fable usage credits that come back early now lift the limit, and chats stopped by it carry on by themselves
